open_obligations: Check that inserted bugs are hard to evaluate in the sense Saunders et al. mean, not only time-consuming.
Read together with McAleese et al.'s negative appendix result on hard contest problems.
Note that the contractor cohort is representative of ChatGPT contractors, not best-possible reviewers.

Check against a cited McAleese et al. passage that the code task is harder for humans to evaluate than topic-based summarisation; the cited passage gives no figures for contractor experience or time per critique.
Note that the cited McAleese et al. result compares LLM-written critiques with human-written critiques, not human evaluation assisted by LLM critiques as in Saunders et al.
out.other_title: Task not hard for humans to evaluate; results may not transfer to harder tasks
out.rationale: Saunders et al. note their base task is not very hard for humans to evaluate, leaving little headroom for assistance; humans take up to about ten minutes, so little speed-up is observed, and positive results on an easier task might not be reproducible on harder tasks. McAleese et al. report that LLM critics (prompted ChatGPT and CriticGPT) catch many more inserted bugs than the human annotators, a cohort representative of the contractors used for ChatGPT; the bugs are inserted, not naturally occurring. The McAleese et al. result compares LLM-written with human-written critiques rather than human evaluation assisted by critiques, and the cited passages do not show that the inserted-bug task is harder for humans to evaluate, so it does not bear on Saunders et al.'s concern, and Saunders et al.'s limitation of their own task does not bear on McAleese et al.'s comparison.
out.scope: proposed SHARES_TOPIC: model help in evaluating model outputs compared with unaided human evaluators, which Saunders et al. discuss for an easy summarisation task and McAleese et al. measure as LLM-written versus human-written code critiques

text: The paper reports that CriticGPT critiques are substantially preferred by contractors over prompted ChatGPT critiques and over human-written critiques from their contractor group, on overall rating. Both LLM critics (prompted ChatGPT and CriticGPT) catch many more inserted bugs than the human annotators; the authors note this contractor cohort is representative of ChatGPT's contractors rather than the best possible humans.
title: CriticGPT critiques preferred over human critiques; LLM critics catch more inserted bugs
